newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal may sell some of its gold reserves - minister.
newsitem.headline: Portugal may sell some of its gold reserves - minister.

text.p: Portugal may sell part of its substantial gold reserves, Economy Minister Augusto Mateus said on Monday.
"Portugal, which holds a large proportion of its reserves in gold...has the possibility to sell part of its gold reserves," Mateus told TSF radio.
But an official central bank source said the Bank of Portugal had received no indication from the government it should sell part of its gold reserves.
A central bank report estimated that the reserves at the end of 1995 stood at about 500 kilos of pure gold, worth some 775 billion escudos ($5 billion).

At the end of September, the central bank had liquid official reserves, which include gold, estimated to be worth 3.3 billion escudos, with the gold valued at market prices, according to the central bank.
"There has been no concrete suggestion from the government," the central bank source said. "The previous statement of the governor (to Expresso weekly) is still valid."

Bank of Portugal governor Antonio De Sousa told Expresso in an interview published on October 6 that Portugal was not planning to sell some of its gold reserves to help it meet convergence criteria for entry to the European single currency.
